banner.provenance: pinned from the 2018 print capture (the settling authority), with the compressed-print capture giving a second independent read of the page - the eight-row table cross-checked cell-by-cell between the two passes; the numeric rating ladder agrees in both passes (10 through 3, one step per row, no contested cells). The one contest is a name, not a number: the AC-4 row third type reads branded mail in the print pass against the compressed banded mail - the print capture own page prose prints banded mail twice in the rare-suits sentence, so the row read is an OCR slip and the name pins as banded mail (a read contradicting its own page does not stand). The type-of-armor names are textual and ride the column comment per the T48 doctrine (the kote and o-yori spellings as printed; the suit rows enumerate multiple types per rating). The corselet-of-laced-armor prose example (armor class 7, equal to studded leather) cross-checks the row-3 rating - the prose itself stays in the open armor prose box. The suits-versus-pieces doctrine and the averaging paragraph stay open; Table 53 (capture p. 95) is deliberately left for the next round

col_comments: the armor class rating, by suit row (capture p. 94). The type-of-armor names ride this comment: 0 None, 1 Shield/kote, 2 Leather or padded armor, 3 Leather, padded armor, & shield/studded leather/leather scale/ring mail, 4 Studded leather, ring mail, leather scale & shield/hide/metal scale/brigandine, 5 Hide, metal scale, brigandine & shield/chain mail, 6 Chain mail & shield/splint mail/banded mail, 7 Splint or banded mail & shield/o-yori - the ratings run 10 through 3, one step per row; the row-6 third type pins as banded mail (the print pass branded read is an OCR slip against its own page prose); a row index outside the table returns the -99 sentinel (capture p. 94).
